**Company Description** American Lithium Energy Corporation is an advanced battery technology company focused on designing and manufacturing high-performance lithium-based energy storage solutions. The company serves a range of applications where reliability, safety, and high energy density are critical, including commercial, industrial, and specialized markets.
Team members collaborate closely across engineering and manufacturing to bring innovative battery products from concept to production. Working at American Lithium Energy Corporation offers opportunities to contribute to cutting-edge power solutions and grow in a fast-paced, technology-driven environment.
**Role Description** The Battery Pack Design and Manufacturing Engineer will be responsible for designing, developing, and optimizing battery pack assemblies from concept through production. Day-to-day tasks include creating mechanical and electrical designs, specifying components and materials, generating drawings and documentation, and coordinating with manufacturing teams to ensure robust, scalable processes.
The role involves hands-on support on the production floor, troubleshooting design and process issues, implementing design for manufacturability (DFM) improvements, and collaborating with cross-functional teams on testing, validation, and quality assurance.
This is a full-time, on-site role based in Carlsbad, CA, requiring regular interaction with engineering, operations, and quality personnel to meet performance, safety, and cost targets.
**Key Responsibilities**
* Battery Pack Design & Development
* Design and develop lithium-ion battery packs
* Develop mechanical design concepts including module structures, busbars, terminals, cooling plates, etc.
* BOM preparation and cost optimization.
* BMS & Electronics Integration
* Work with BMS teams for hardware and firmware integration.
* Define protection parameters: OVP, UVP, OCP, OTP, short circuit limits, SOC/SOH algorithms.
* Support SMbus and CAN communication development
* Testing & Validation
* Develop DVP&R (Design Validation Plan & Report) for battery packs.
* Conduct electrical, thermal, mechanical, vibration, and environmental tests.
* Analyze test data and generate technical reports.
* Perform failure analysis (cell, module, pack-level failures).
* Prototype Development
* Oversee prototype pack assembly and testing.
* Collaborate with production for smooth transfer from design stage to mass manufacturing.
* Validate fixtures, jigs, and assembly processes.
* Standards & Certification
* Work with purchase, quality, production, and service teams.
* Support customer technical discussions
* Benchmark competitor battery packs and technologies.
* Supervise pack assembly and manufacturing technicians and operators
**Qualifications**
* Strong background in Design Engineering and Product Design for battery packs or related electromechanical systems.
* Knowledge of Manufacturing Processes with experience translating designs into efficient, repeatable production methods.
* Experience in Manufacturing Engineering, including process optimization, tooling, and production line support.
* Solid foundation in Mechanical Engineering, including materials, structural design, thermal considerations, and CAD tools.
* Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
* Experience with battery pack design, lithium-ion cells, safety standards, and validation/testing protocols is highly beneficial.
* Ability to read and create technical drawings, specifications, and documentation with attention to detail and quality.
* Strong problem-solving skills, ability to work collaboratively on-site, and effective communication with cross-functional teams.
* Supervising skills

Maintain a mindset of continuous improvement to keep our production-related processes ever evolving.
Establish and share the vision towards a common goal while holding self and others accountable.
Primary focus is to Lead Rocket Motor/Spaceship fabrication and assembly. As a Supervisor, your role is to help refine and improve the production flow, equipment, and tools to create an efficient, organized, and lean factory. Organize daily tasks to meet milestones, in alignment with manufacturing schedule, and drive the overall performance of the manufacturing plan.
To be successful, this supervisory role will require collaboration across teams and all functions of planning, scheduling, demands, and assembly to properly support the build schedule by means of identifying tooling, materials, resources, planning, and product definition to ensure a seamless transition from paper to reality.

** Onsite Monday through Friday Day (6:00am – 4:30pm)
**Potential Future Work Schedules
** Onsite Monday through Friday Night (4:00pm - 2:30am)
Onsite Thursday through Monday Day (6:00am – 4:30pm)

**

* Lead and manage a team of technicians including all performance management related tasks and team development
* Oversight of Assembling Spaceship/ Rocket Motor components from start to completion in a fast-paced Mfg. Environment
* Influences technical projects, technicians, or interdepartmental functions to achieve goals or solve problems
* Continuously improve procedures, processes, and efficiencies
* Drive safety behavior and Foreign Object Debris (FOD) awareness/prevention; ensure adherence to regulatory protocols and rules
* Coach, train, and transfer expertise to your team to drive projects to completions
* Work closely with Build Management to forecast completion dates and day to day updates
* Collaborate effectively with Manufacturing, Design and Quality Engineers to ensure our vehicles meet our standards for design and quality
* Prioritize work based on production schedule, organizational goals, and metrics
* Utilize your overall general knowledge of Composite and similar Manufacturing skills to produce a high performing Hybrid Rocket
* Work with manufacturing software system to manage material and product review process
**Required Skills And Experience
**
* Relevant education, such as trade school or Associate’s degree; and /or equivalent technical work experience
* Minimum of six years’ experience in an aerospace or equivalent high-reliability field with three years of leading others and/ or demonstrated ability to lead and train on technical concepts
* Experience with aircraft manufacturing with composite and/or metallic airframes
* Experience in assembly, integration, and handling of large products, assembling large tight tolerance structures
* Extensive experience and/or training in lean manufacturing principles and leading or participating in process improvement workshops
* Ability to read and interpret drawings, blueprints, and/or models on paper or digital
* Demonstrated computer and analytical skills including proficiency in MS Excel, manufacturing software or related programs and dashboards
**Preferred Skills And Experience
**
* Airframe & Power plant (A&P) training preferred
* Knowledge of lean manufacturing (Kaizen/Six Sigma) philosophies and tools a plus
* Working knowledge of configuration management practices and quality management processes
* Proficient in interpreting engineering models, drawings, specifications, written/digital work
* Strong analytical skills, combined with a strong commercial acumen to measure the potential impact of each decision
* Ability to ensure effective collaboration across teams
* Ability to work independently and cross‐functionally
* Set clear objectives and milestones
* Communicate clearly and with transparency
* Lead by example in strong safety forward thinking, practice good housekeeping, tool control, recognizing the importance of properly handling hazardous materials and, chemicals
* Familiar with the use of personal protective equipment (PPE)
* Ability to lift up to 50 pounds
